headline: holding $0.091 to $0.094 support after the SEC letter
lede: Canton Coin (CC) price, chart levels and three scenarios for the week ahead, plus what's happening with CNTN stock. Plain English, no hype.
summary: Canton Coin is at $0.0927 (about R1.53), down about 5% this week and 24% this month. Price is back at the $0.091 to $0.094 support zone for the second week, even after good news: the SEC staff's no-action letter on 3 November and DTCC going live on Canton. The network now burns about 70% as much CC as it mints, better than last week but still net new supply. CNTN stock rose about 6% to $2.06, and tokenized CNTN shares made their first trades on 4 November.
summary_plain: Canton Coin at $0.0927, down about 5% this week. Support $0.091 to $0.094, resistance $0.0995. SEC no-action letter, DTCC live, tokenized CNTN trading. Scenarios and CNTN stock for 8 November 2026.
snapshot: 40.02 billion CC, no maximum, still growing
snapshot_note: Snapshot 8 November 2026 from CoinGecko, cross checked with the Kraken CC/USD price ($0.0927).
chart_alt: Canton Coin daily closes from 19 October to 8 November 2026, falling from about $0.105 to $0.093, with support at $0.091 to $0.094 and resistance at $0.0995 and $0.105
changed: 📉 Price slipped from $0.0962 to $0.0927. The 8 November price is the lowest of the past three weeks.
📜 SEC staff issued a no-action letter on 3 November treating CC as a digital commodity. CC rose about 4% that day, then gave it back. It is staff's enforcement view, not a binding ruling.
🏦 DTCC's tokenization service went live on Canton on 28 October and an Uber and HSBC pilot was announced, yet the CC chart barely reacted.
🔥 Burn is catching up: about 15 million CC burned per day against about 22 million minted, down from roughly 2 to 1 last week.
📈 CNTN stock rose from $1.98 to $2.06 (about +6% on the week) and tokenized CNTN shares made their first trades on 4 November.
technicals: Lower highs since February, and since 22 October ($0.112, $0.105, $0.099)
Roughly $0.13 (not re-checked this week; price is far below)
About level with its signal line, both below zero (bearish but flattening)
Quiet: about $9 million a day, versus $24 to $25 million on the 3 to 4 November spike
Open interest and funding could not be read this week (Coinglass blocks automated readers)
levels: 20 October high and where the 21 to 22 October rally stalled
5 November close and the 20 day average
3 and 7 November closes, buyers stepped in each time
Last week's support and a low-volume gap below
scenarios: Room toward $0.105, then the 50 day average near $0.112
Sideways chop while the market digests the SEC letter and burn data
Opens $0.088, with little support below that
fundamentals: 🔥 Burn vs mint: one independent analysis (CantonNews, 8 November) finds about 15.2 million CC burned and 21.9 million minted per day, so about 6.7 million CC of net new supply daily. Universal burn (CIP-0129, approved) still starts around Q1 2027. Four nodes make up 87.5% of the burn.
🏦 Banks: DTCC's node bought network traffic once (787,155 CC on 26 October) and other big names bought none in the period studied. The network is being used, CC mostly is not yet.
📜 Regulation and ecosystem: SEC staff no-action letter (3 November), six new Canton Foundation members, Splice 0.9.4 MainNet upgrade due 9 November, new grant proposals. No unlocks or ETF news found.
cntn_notes: CNTN is Canton Strategic Holdings, a Nasdaq company that holds about 3.7 billion CC. It is not Digital Asset, the private company that built Canton Network.

Tokenized CNTN shares are live: the first four trades ($30,296 in total) ran on TSV LLC on 4 November, with Fairmint as transfer agent. Only verified participants can trade, and South African access has not been announced.
You can buy CNTN through Interactive Brokers from most countries, or any US broker. See the step-by-step guide.
bottom_line: 📉 Price is back on support at $0.091 to $0.094 despite good news. A close below $0.091 would be the level to respect.
🔥 Burn is closing the gap with minting but supply still grows, and bank use of CC itself is thin.
👀 Watch the Splice 0.9.4 upgrade and whether tokenized CNTN opens to more buyers.
